Serbs are gods", and one ugly thing remained because on the third or fourth truck, I do not remember, in the front there was a big head of a cow which was cut off and placed on the grill up front and that is how they were going up towards Benkovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you also see troops accompanying these vehicles?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How were they dressed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were in regular military clothes, some of them in multi-coloured.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were they armed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you recall what kinds of arms the troops had?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The military had automatic weapons with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: From what direction did this convoy arrive?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This last column that went towards Mrakovica was a column coming from Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Previous columns, had they also come from Prijedor or from another direction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were from the direction of Prijedor and from Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: On May 24th, the day of the attack on Kozarac, were you at Rajkovici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where in Rajkovici were you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Rajkovici, not Rajkovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you at a particular location?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was in the village of Rajkovici which is on the road towards Mrakovica from Kozarac. On the left at Risvo Hrmanovic(?) built a hotel there and that is where we were.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were many of your police colleagues there as well as police chief Osme Didovic and Becir Medunjanin, the Secretary of the National Defence in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did Becir Medunjanin speak on a radio to any Serb official?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you recall who he spoke to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Becir Medunjanin talked with Radmilo Zeljaja over the line from the car in Rajkovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What was Becir Medunjanin trying to tell Radmilo Zeljaja?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He tried to say what to do. He basically requested not to start, because Becir knew what was going to happen and he was all but crying over the line, but Radmilo Zeljaja said, "Becir, it is too late now".

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: About what time of the day was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was around 11.30 on Sunday.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: About what time did the shelling begin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sunday, the same day, 1.30, the first shells started falling.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After the shells began to fall, did you and your colleague seek shelter in the cellar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Then that night did you go to a nearby village and spend the night?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The next morning did you come back to the same shelter for a period of time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Then did you go to your home in Kozarac to find your family and take them to the forest?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: From the forest that afternoon did you again return to your home in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When you were in Kozarac that afternoon did you have binoculars?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you able to see what was happening in the area of Kozarusa?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could see it perfectly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What was happening in that area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From Kozarusa, that means from Prijedor, all houses were burning, the first tank that you could see in Susici near Limenka. That was the name for the bus stop. It just remained that name.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you see not only tanks but Serbian troops moving through the area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That same afternoon, Monday afternoon, were you in the centre part of Kozarac and did you speak with police colleagues?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did they tell you that a plan had been reached or an agreement had been reached to surrender?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What was the understanding of what was to happen to the people who surrendered under that agreement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The agreement was, apparently, to go to Prijedor, to the sports ground, for about three days. That was the information given us.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After three days what was supposed to happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Who knew?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you decide not to surrender, that you did not want to give yourself up into Serb hands at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In that event it was difficult to find a solution, what one should do. The wife and children were at home and I was down there. Kozarac is on fire. The shells are falling. I decided and Hamdija, we started to go back to my place.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Hamdija is your brother?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My cousin.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: As a police officer, had you been issued a weapon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that time we turned in our weapons in front of the police station in Kozarac, the ones that we had taken from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Then you went to back your home in Stari Grad with Hamdija?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was that the last you would see of your police colleagues until you later arrived in Omarska where you would again see some of those who survived?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The next day, the third day of the attack, did you change your mind about surrendering?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was no other reason. It was burning from all sides. That was Tuesday in the evening. We had nothing, no other option, but to start going towards the Serb Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you and your family go into Kozarac to surrender in the early evening on Tuesday?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were there soldiers and military equipment in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There could have been more than what I saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were there tanks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: As you proceeded down Marsala Tita, at some point were the men in the column that you were with ordered to walk in a different direction from the women?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we arrived to that column at the bottom of the Marsala Tita Street, which is the main street to the sports ground, that is where men were separated to the left and women and children to the right, and right away it was there that it started, the beatings and the abuse.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So the men were supposed to walk in the direction of Banja Luka and the women in the direction of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How far did the men begin to proceed down the main road toward Banja Luka before they were stopped?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We did not go far. As people were arriving they were lying down on the ground, hands like this, and then as we were lining up, as we were arriving.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So you were told, you and others, to lie face down with your hands behind your head on the ground?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What happened when you did?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then right away the beatings started there. It was not allowed for me to lie down in a normal way. As people were arriving, they were being beaten as they were lying down.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: About what time of the day was this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we arrived to the asphalt it was dusk.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How long did you and the others stay there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We, men, were lying down there until 1.30, after midnight.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: At about 1.30 did buses arrive?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where did the buses take you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They put us in the buses there, but that was abnormal. They were pushing us, they were beating us and they started moving towards Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where did they stop?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We stopped in Keraterm.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you ever get off the buses in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we arrived in Keraterm, the buses turned around and parked and we remained there until the next day in the evening, that was Wednesday, until 9.30 Wednesday night, in the buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you ever permitted to get off the buses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You were not allowed to look out from the buses, let alone get off.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After you had been there until about 9.30 in the evening, where did the buses take you then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that time we did not know where we were going, but we started at 9.30. It was night. You could see a little bit through the window into the night, they do not see if you look. But when we were leaving Keraterm, we were not going either to Banja Luka, Bosanski Novi, we were going in the direction of Tomasica, and arrived in Omarska and we only found that out the next day.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: About what time did you arrive in Omarska? How long had that trip taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: According to me, that trip was supposed to take 40 minutes, but we went from 9.30. Some buses arrived at 2.30, I think, and later. I think it was 2.30 when we arrived in Omarska, we could have arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When your bus and the other buses arrived were guards waiting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: As prisoners got off the buses, were the guards waiting in a particular position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can you describe that, please, and tell us what happened as prisoners left the buses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we were stepping off the bus, they put a cordon of Serbian soldiers and we passed between them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: As you passed between them, what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The hands were over the head. If you could walk faster you got less, those who walked slower got more.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When you refer to "less" or "more", are you referring to blows and kicks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Beatings, yes, blows, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where were you held when you first arrived in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I arrived in Omarska, I went upstairs, up the stairs, then to the right. That is No. 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You went up the stairs in which building? May I ask you this, there was one building in which the kitchen was housed, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was not there where the kitchen was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So you were in the other larger building, sometimes referred to as the hangar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When you entered the hangar building, did you take the first stairway to the left?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was by the staircase and to the right. That is where I was in that room until the interrogation, No. 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So when you got to the top of the staircase you went right and that is where No. 15 was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was that a room that was partially separated by an area on one side where there were showers and an area on the other side where there was a wash room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As you enter that room, to the left are showers and to the right a wash basin or something, and it was connected. That was in the middle.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You said you remained there until you were interrogated. How long were you in room 15?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Four or five days.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you receive any food during that time from the camp guards or officials?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were there some prisoners who managed to purchase biscuits or small amounts of food?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you remember what the price was for biscuits during that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: More than excellent.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How much did it cost to buy a pack of biscuits or cigarettes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 100 marks, two biscuits and a box of cigarettes, or the other way round, two boxes of cigarettes and one biscuit.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After four or five days or so you indicated you were interrogated. Before you entered the interrogation room, were you required to say anything in particular?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Would you repeat it, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Certainly. Were you required to say anything before you were permitted actually to enter the interrogation, the room where the interrogation was conducted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I was entering the interrogation room the guard who escorted me came up to the room. I knocked and I said, "Good day". I had to return because I had not said it properly. I did not greet properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you instructed with what the proper greeting was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, when the guard in the corridor told me what I was expected to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you say it and can you tell us what that was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You had to say it. It is not whether I could say it. I had to say, "God help you heroes", and not "hello" or "good day".

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: During the course of your interrogation were you struck and kicked?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you kicked in a way which left a long-lasting injury to your leg?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What kind of injury did you have?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is an injury I have on my left leg. I had thrombosis of the left leg when I arrived from Omarska to Trnopolje. I was given something to put on it and I went for treatment. I still suffer the effects and many, many others.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After the interrogation what part of the camp were you held in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We called it "hangar". I do not think that area has a number, a garage, a hangar.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was it also upstairs in the hangar building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: To get to this room did you use the same staircase you used to get to room 15, or did you use another staircase?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not use the same staircase. I had to use another one.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: To get to this room that you were placed in after the interrogation, did you go through the entrance and pass that first stairway and then turn right walking by the toilet until you got to a room in which the staircase was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is where I went. It is through the hangar and that is what we called it, where the dump trucks were.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: OK. To get into the room where the staircase was, did you go through a glass door?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were there prisoners in that room before you got to the staircase?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were there lockers on both sides of that small room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is what I remember well, where people were lying down, yes, a small locker, working type.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were there also prisoners on top of the lockers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were there prisoners on the staircase?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When you got to the top of the staircase did you then go right to get to the area where you were held after the interrogation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You indicated that that particular room to the right of the staircase, as far as you remember, did not have a number?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, we called it garage, room, whatever you like.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you consider your room just that particular area where those four walls were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What else did the area you considered your room consist of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the entrance on the staircase, the pedestal, other stairs, then upstairs to the right, to the left, that room where I was and downstairs, and there was yet another smaller piece where there were and we called it all one.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did the prisoners in that area go to lunch 30 prisoners at a time, basically one group after another from that area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Once you entered the glass doors and started up the stairs and went upstairs, were there guards in that area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Could prisoners move around from the upstairs to the downstairs and talk to other prisoners, for example?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Only those two rooms which we considered to be one, not further.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Depending on the shift, was it possible sometimes to go outside on to the floor of the hangar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it only depended on the shift. If a shift was a good one we could go downstairs from that room there, that was one room adjacent to the other. There was a long wooden bench and we could sit there and talk, and we could go into that room. It all depended on the will of the guards.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sir, can I ask you briefly to describe the general conditions in Omarska during the period of time you were held there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I only do not know if it bears description, the way it was. From beatings, killing, hunger, water, living conditions, a bath after 53 days as if you washed the truck, that is how we washed and many, many, but beating, typhoid and many, many other things. I came to Trnopolje and I had lost 35 kilogrammes during the Omarska camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you transferred to Trnopolje camp when the main group of prisoners were transferred from Omarska to either Manjaca or Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you remain in Trnopolje until October 1st?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where were you first held when you arrived in Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was in the wire until I managed, that is one cannot say about lice, filth, and after that I found a little room in the school, a little room for me, a little space for me in the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was it in the school that you stayed until you were transferred from Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were there guards in Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: More than I thought.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were they stationed at various places and around the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After you arrived at -- at the time you arrived at Trnopolje did you have any idea what had happened to your family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you primarily interested in finding out some information about what happened to your family or determining whether somebody might be in a position to give you information?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was my only purpose to find that out.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you try to make a point when you could of looking around to see whether or not there were people you knew from before the war who might be able to give you some information on your family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: During the course of looking around for people who might be able to provide you with some scrap of information about your family, did you see any Serbs you knew from before the war in Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Who did you see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Zdravko Torbica, Goran Babic, Dule Tadic, Milos Radulovic, and many, many others. That is, the only reason was to look who had, that is what interested me most, who was there, whom could I approach to enquire about my family, and that is why I was curious who was there so as to learn something.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Previously you mentioned a Serb from Kozarac by the name of Goran Borovnica. Did you ever see him in Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was Goran Borovnica. There were very many others.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you know a man named Tepo Vidovic before the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Tepo Vidovic, Goran Vidovic, I am telling you there were many, many. I did not give you all the names.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When you saw these men, were they dressed in military uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All but one.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And who was not in military uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Goran Babic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What was he wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Police clothes, that is he was a policeman in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were these men whom you mentioned armed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sir, do you recall the first time you saw Dule Tadic in Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where were you that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Could I briefly have Exhibit 277A presented to the witness? (Handed). Sir, do you recognise what is shown in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Very well I recognise it, except there are some changes here compared to when I was here last.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: May that be placed on the Elmo? First of all, Mr. Arifagic, what does it show?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This the school at Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What are the changes you noticed from the time you were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I was there these here logs were not there. This addition here, this part here, did not exist. This was added subsequently. When, I would not know that, but it was not there then.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may this photograph be marked as Exhibit 310 for identification, please. There is a copy for the Court. Sir, does this photograph show the school from a different angle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is the self-same school, but not from the same side. The entrance into the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would tender 310 for admission.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 310 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: May that be placed briefly on the Elmo. Sir, can we see in this photograph the approximate position where you were on the first occasion you saw Dule Tadic in Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can you show us where that would be?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated on the photograph].

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So, you were -- is that upstairs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you watching out of that window?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you recall about what time of the day it was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Afternoon it was. The time exactly I did not look.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you remember approximately what period of time during your confinement in Trnopolje that occurred?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I came from Omarska I was weak. I was lying upstairs, but afterwards, after some 15, 13 days must have been.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When you first saw Dule Tadic where was he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said I was most trying to see somebody I knew whom I could tell that I was there, so as to learn something about the family. I could walk a little better then, so I walked up and down the school and it was by chance that I reached that window and when I was there I saw Dusko. He was moving towards this, in this direction, that is behind the school. That was all very brief.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So when you first saw him he was inside the fenced area we see in the photograph, somewhere near the sidewalk and moving toward the school but at an angle toward the left side of the school as we look at it, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, to the left. Yes, he was moving there, towards that corner there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was he with anyone else or was he by himself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was alone.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you remember what he was wearing on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Whenever I saw him he was in clothes with weapons and that is with automatic short weapons that we called an automatic rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The answer we received indicated simply that he was "in clothes with weapons". Do you recall what kind of clothes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Camouflage clothes, those multi-coloured camouflage.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Let me ask you then about the next occasion on which you saw Dusko Tadic. Where were you on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then I was in front of the school downstairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Again, do you happen to remember what time of the day it was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was also afternoon 2 or 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Let me ask to have Exhibit 277 placed on the Elmo, 277A, which shows a slightly wider section of the area. Can we see in this photograph the approximate position you were in on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can you point that out for us, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated on the photograph]. Here in front of the school there was a kind of a pedestal where one could sit down and have a smoke.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That would be in the approximate position of the figures or people we see in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where was Dule Tadic when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here on the inside, here, here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You are indicating on the inside of that fenced area some metres away from the corner which we see at the bottom left of the picture. On that occasion was he by himself or was he with anyone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. No, he was with Goran Babic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When you saw Goran Babic and Dule Tadic what were they doing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Standing.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In what direction or directions were they facing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were facing one another.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Relative to your position or relative to where you were, how were they positioned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One had his back to this side, and that is he was facing the asphalt here and the other one was looking in that direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So one was positioned basically with his back to the street and the other with his back to the field or school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Facing the field, not the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What were Goran Babic and Dule Tadic doing? Were they just standing there? Were they talking? Could you tell what they were doing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were only talking, but I did not want to see them, so I turned my back and went upstairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Why did you not want to stay in the position where you were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because we knew each other too well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you concerned about what might happen to you if either one of them saw you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was the first thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I guess this would be an appropriate time.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We will adjourn until tomorrow at 10 a.m. (5.30 p.m.). (The court adjourned until the following day). 18
